title: The ledger lock shares the project lock's code
lead: `store.project_lock` and `ops.ledger_lock` take their flock through one `store.file_lock(path)` helper, and the `.slicer/` listing in docs/commands.md describes the legacy ledger correctly.
findings_note: s298 review 2026-10-16: ledger_lock copies project_lock; docs listing wording
boundary: **Not in this slice:** any change to lock timeouts, error codes or where the lock files live.

sections.heading: Why
sections.body: The s298 review (2026-10-16) accepted two small debts. `ops.ledger_lock` copies the flock-and-deadline loop of `store.project_lock`, calls the private `store._lock_timeout()`, and words its timeout message differently, so the two locks can drift. And the `.slicer/` listing in `docs/commands.md` (about line 390) says the legacy ledger is "no longer written in a git repo", but a project below the worktree root still writes it.

sections.heading: Files
sections.body:
- `src/slicer/store.py`: `file_lock(path)`, a context manager with the flock loop, timeout and `locked` error that `project_lock` has now; `project_lock` calls it.
- `src/slicer/ops.py`: `ledger_lock` calls `store.file_lock` and no longer uses `store._lock_timeout`.
- `docs/commands.md`, the `relay-runs.jsonl` line: "read in a git repo; still written for a project below the worktree root and outside git".
- `tests/test_relay_run.py` or the existing lock tests.

sections.heading: Failing tests
sections.body: - `test_LedgerLock_Held_TimesOutWithLockedCode`: a held shared-ledger lock gives `locked` with the same message shape as the project lock.

sections.heading: Implement
sections.body:
1. Write the test; extract the helper; keep every existing lock test green.
2. Fix the docs line. Mutation-check (break the timeout in `file_lock`: both lock tests fail).

sections.heading: Check
sections.body: - `python3.12 tests/affected.py --run`, then the full suite. `slicer check` passes.

sections.heading: Git
sections.body: One commit on the slice branch; the owner lands it.
